title: Document pipeline — how is the batch orchestrated?
description: Three variants of the same pipeline. The processing script is shared; only what starts it changes. Switch the active variant from the status bar: nothing is written. Record decision is what commits a choice.

decisions.title: What starts the processing of each PDF?

options.label: A — direct script
options.summary: A Python script lists the inbox and processes each new PDF, by hand or on a schedule.
pros: Nothing to deploy: runs wherever Python runs
cons: Someone (or a scheduler) must start it

costs.label: A small Linux VM to run it nightly
costs.note: 0 when it runs on a machine you already have

options.label: B — Blob event + Function
options.summary: Each new blob triggers an Azure Function that processes it.
pros: Processes each PDF as soon as it arrives
cons: A Function App to deploy and monitor

costs.label: Functions Consumption plan, a few thousand runs a month
costs.price: first 1 million executions a month free, then 0.20 USD per million

options.label: C — Data Factory pipeline
options.summary: A Data Factory pipeline with a storage event trigger calls the processing.
pros: Monitoring, retries and lineage in Data Factory Studio
cons: A factory and its Git folder to create first

costs.label: Orchestration, about 3,000 activity runs a month
costs.price: about 1 USD per 1,000 activity runs (Azure integration runtime)
